3.  Purpose of this Technical Advisory 

(a)  The purpose of this Technical Advisory is to provide guidance to internal and external 

stakeholders on the implementation and administration of the Special Consumption Tax 

(SCT) on Non‑Alcoholic Sweetened Beverages (NASBs) arising from amendments to 

the  General  Consumption  Tax  (GCT)  Act  and  its  administration  through  the  Excise 

Duty Act.   

(b) This was announced in the 2026-2027 Revenue Measures tabled in the House by the 

MoFPS,  the  Honourable  Fayval  Williams  and  implemented  by  The  General 

Consumption  Tax  (Amendment  of  Schedules)  Order,  2026,  Resolution  (see 

Appendix 1) approved in the House of Representatives on April 28, 2026. 

4.  Policy Objective 

(a)  The SCT on NASBs is intended to: 

•  apply a consumption‑based tax to non-alcoholic sweetened beverages aligned with 

existing excise regime (e.g. alcohol and tobacco); 

•  encourage reformulation toward lower sweetener content; 

•  address public‑health externalities linked to sugar consumption; and 

Advisory #: 052026/01/GCT-TA 
DISCLAIMER: This Advisory is a guide only and is not a substitute for the GCT Act, the GCT 
Regulations, the Excise Duty Act, the Excise Duty Regulations or any other relevant legislation.

•  strengthen revenue mobilisation in a neutral manner across domestic and imported 

products. 

(b) The tax is imposed at a specific rate of J$0.22 per gram of added sweetener  

(c)  The SCT on NASBs forms part of the Government’s fiscal and public‑health policy 

measures. 

5.  Scope of this Technical Advisory 

(a)  This Technical Advisory is not a legally binding document, but is intended to provide 

guidance and clarity to all manufacturers of prescribed goods, tax practioners and TAJ 

officers  in  understanding  the  tax  implications  of  the  introduction  of  SCT  on  the 

Non‑Alcoholic Sweetened Beverages. 

(b)  The  document  is  not  meant  to  be  comprehensive  and  does  not  provide  a  definitive 

response  for  all  possible  issues  impacting  the  introduction  of  the  SCT  on  the 

Non‑Alcoholic Sweetened Beverages. 

(c)  This  document  is  subject  to  change  without  notice.  The  document  is  based  on  the 

legislation  as  it  stood  when  the  technical  advisory  was  published.  Each  person’s 

specific circumstances should be considered independent of the other.

8. 

Implementation Date 

The effective date of the legislation is May 1, 2026.  

9.  Scope of Application 

9.1.  Products in Scope 

(a)  The SCT applies to Non‑Alcoholic Sweetened Beverages, namely: 

•  Beverages containing less than 0.5% alcohol by volume (ABV); 

•  Commercially produced, packaged, sealed, and ready for retail sale; 

• 

Intended for direct human consumption without further dilution or preparation; 

and 

•  To which added sweeteners have been incorporated during manufacture. 

(b) Products in scope include, but are not limited to: 

•  carbonated soft drinks; 

•  non‑carbonated sweetened beverages (iced teas, flavoured waters, lemonades); 

•  energy and sports drinks; and 

•  certain fermented beverages (e.g. kombucha) below the ABV threshold and not 

otherwise taxed on alcohol content. 

Advisory #: 052026/01/GCT-TA 
DISCLAIMER: This Advisory is a guide only and is not a substitute for the GCT Act, the GCT 
Regulations, the Excise Duty Act, the Excise Duty Regulations or any other relevant legislation.

9.2.  Exclusions and Exemptions 

(a)  The SCT does not apply to: 

• 

liquid whole milk and skimmed milk; 

•  100% juices with no added sweeteners; 

•  exported NASBs or shipped as stores; and 

•  beverages sweetened at the point of sale (e.g. restaurants, cafés). 

(b) Concentrates,  syrups,  powders,  and  drink  mixes  intended  for  reconstitution  are 

outside scope at this stage. 

10.  Manufacturers in Scope  

A manufacturer who: 

•  has been duly registered and licensed prior to May 1, 2026 must account for SCT 

on NASBs produced or in storage as of that date.  

•  has been duly registered and licensed after May 1, 2026 must account for SCT on 

NASBs produced or in storage as of the date of the license issued by TAJ. 

•  makes a change to the pricing of NASBs on or after May 1, 2026, on account of 

the imposition of the SCT on NASBs, will be liable for the SCT payable, 

notwithstanding the registration/licensing status. 

11.  Administration of NASB under the Excise Framework  

11.1. 

Excise Duty Act & Excise Regulations Act 

Although  legislated  under  the  GCT  Act,  SCT  on  NASBs  is  administered  using  the 

Excise  Duty  Act  and  Regulations.  SCT  is  not  self‑assessed;  liability  is  determined 

immediately before removal from a factory or, private excise warehouse. 

Advisory #: 052026/01/GCT-TA 
DISCLAIMER: This Advisory is a guide only and is not a substitute for the GCT Act, the GCT 
Regulations, the Excise Duty Act, the Excise Duty Regulations or any other relevant legislation.

11.1.1. 

Functions of Tax Administration 

Under the Excise Duty Act, TAJ is responsible for: 

• 

licensing of manufacturers and approval of excise private warehouses; 

•  supervision and control of manufacturing and warehousing operations; 

•  verification of production, stock, and removals; 

•  assessment and confirmation of SCT liability; 

•  audit, sampling, and testing (including use of the Government Chemist or BSJ); 

•  enforcement actions, including penalties and seizures where applicable. 

11.2. 

Licensing Requirements  

(a)  Under sections 24, 25 and 29 of the Excise Duty Act and paragraphs 16 and 17 of 

the Excise Duty Regulations, all NASB manufacturers must: 

•  obtain a license to manufacture excisable goods; (See Appendices 2 to 4) 

•  have approved factory premises or excise private warehouses; 

•  comply with inspection, security, and record‑keeping requirements; and 

•  maintain  approved  systems  for  measuring  and  recording  production  and 

removals. 

(b) Licensing  is  conditional  on  site  inspections  and  compliance  with  excise  control 

standards. 

11.3. 

Registration and Filing under the GCT Act 

11.3.1. Registration  

NASB manufacturers must: 

•  be registered taxpayers under the GCT Act; (see Appendix 5) 

• 

register NASBs as prescribed goods subject to SCT; 

•  complete product/SKU registration to support sugar‑based calculations. 

Advisory #: 052026/01/GCT-TA 
DISCLAIMER: This Advisory is a guide only and is not a substitute for the GCT Act, the GCT 
Regulations, the Excise Duty Act, the Excise Duty Regulations or any other relevant legislation.

11.3.2. Filing and Payment 

•  SCT liability arises immediately before goods are removed: 

o  from a factory or private excise warehouse for local consumption;  

•  Exported NASBs are zero-rated for SCT immediately before goods are 

removed, in accordance with excise controls. 

•  SCT Return is to be filed monthly, using the Form 4C Return, (see Appendix 

6) due on or before the last working day after the end of the taxable period 

11.4. 

Obligations of Manufacturers 

(a)  Manufacturers are required to: 

•  accurately declare added sweetener content per product and SKU; 

•  maintain comprehensive records under section 91 of the EDA, including: 

o  product formulations and variations (including technical datasheets); 
o  raw material accounts; 
o  production and batch records; 
o  stock and warehouse records; 
o  removal and delivery documentation; and 
o  SCT duty calculation records; 

•  make records available for inspection under sections section 92 of the EDA;  

• 

facilitate sampling and testing by TAJ; 

•  apply for approval for destruction, spoilage, or wastage where applicable; and 

•  ensure SCT is incorporated into the cost base for GCT valuation, i.e. the SCT 

payable forms part of the value of taxable supplies for GCT purposes 

(b) Goods removed  for staff use, promotions, or  internal consumption are treated as 

removals for home consumption and attract SCT unless otherwise approved. 

Advisory #: 052026/01/GCT-TA 
DISCLAIMER: This Advisory is a guide only and is not a substitute for the GCT Act, the GCT 
Regulations, the Excise Duty Act, the Excise Duty Regulations or any other relevant legislation.

11.5. 

Spoilage, Destruction, and Returns 

11.5.1. Destruction or Spoilage of NASBs 

(a)  Where NASBs: 

•  become spoilt or unfit for use; or 

• 

fail to meet trade specifications, 

(b) Section 16(4) of the Excise Duty Act allows the Commissioner, at his discretion, 

to: 

•  permit the return of goods to the factory or private excise warehouse; 

•  approve destruction or other disposal under supervision; and 

•  credit or refund SCT paid in respect of those goods. 

11.5.2. Loss of control or traceability 

(a)  To the extent that NASBs are already with an unrelated third party (for example, an 

independent retailer or end customer), the Commissioner General must be satisfied 

that:  

• 

the goods being returned were manufactured and recorded under excise control; 

•  proof that SCT was actually paid on the goods in question;  

• 

• 

the  goods  were  not  partially  sold,  opened,  or  mixed  with  any  other  non-

excisable stock; and 

they will be properly destroyed or disposed of under the supervision of Excise 

(b) Manufacturers must apply in writing to the Commissioner General and obtain approval 

before destruction. 

Advisory #: 052026/01/GCT-TA 
DISCLAIMER: This Advisory is a guide only and is not a substitute for the GCT Act, the GCT 
Regulations, the Excise Duty Act, the Excise Duty Regulations or any other relevant legislation.

 TECHNICAL ADVISORY 
“Tax Treatment: Non-Alcoholic Sweetened Beverages”      
  Revenue Measure 2026/2027 

11.5.3. What Is Not Covered by the Excise Duty Act 

(a)  The Act does not provide relief where goods are returned solely because of: 

•  Overstocking 

•  Poor sales 

•  Commercial recall without quality defect 

•  Change in branding, pricing, or marketing 

•  Expiry due to normal shelf-life without defect 

•  Goods removed from factory or private excise warehouse before the effective 

date of legislation 

(b) In the above cases: 

•  The manufacturer may issue a commercial refund or credit to the retailer 

•  SCT remains payable 

•  No statutory refund or drawback arises under the Excise Duty Act 

12.  Calculation of the Tax 

The  tax  is  imposed  at  the  rate  of  J$0.22  per  gram  of  added  sweetener  contained  in  a 

NASB. 

•  The SCT is to be applied to: 

o 
o 

 the number of grams of added sugar contained in the NASB; 

the weight in grams of non‑nutritive sweeteners contained in the NASB.  

Records of added sweeteners in the NASB including the weight, must be maintained on 

the Technical Datasheet.

13.  Compliance Approach  

(a)  TAJ will administer the SCT using: 

• 

risk‑based onboarding and audits; 

•  on‑site, process and post‑audit verification; 

• 

independent testing of declared sweetener content; and 

•  collaboration with Jamaica Customs Agency and regulators. 

14.  Transitional Arrangements 

(a)  A time‑bound transition period will apply to allow manufacturers to achieve full 

compliance with registration, licensing, warehousing, and reporting requirements.  

(b) Activities in this period will include 

•  additional time for the completion of licensing and registration 

•  additional time for systems alignment and reporting readiness 

•  stakeholders onboard and training 

(c)  TAJ will provide: 

•  Guidance through webinars and advisories 

•  Ongoing support during implementation 

15.  Practical Compliance Steps 

Manufacturers of NASBs should: 

•  Register for SCT under the GCT Act 

•  Apply  for  applicable  excise  licenses  by  submitting  a  letter  of  intent  (see 

Appendix 2, 3 & 4) 

•  Register all SKUs

•  Declare all sweetener content 

•  Establish and maintain internal tracking systems 

•  File monthly SCT returns 

•  Maintain all supporting documentation 

16.  Summary 

(a)  Manufacturers are encouraged to: 

• 

review product formulations and labels; 

•  ensure  excise  licenses  and  private  excise  warehouse  approvals  (where 

applicable) are in place; 

•  strengthen internal controls;  

•  strengthen record‑keeping systems; and 

•  engage early with TAJ where clarification is required. 

(b) This Technical Advisory reflects the administrative framework for SCT on NASBs 

and should be read together with the GCT Act, GCT Regulations, Excise Duty Act 

and, Excise Duty Regulations, and any subsequent advisory issued by TAJ. 

(c)  The GCT threshold as mentioned in section 27(1) (i) the GCT Act and regulation 

2(3)  under  the  GCT  Regulation  does  not  impact  the  registration  of  a  registered 

taxpayer for the manufacturers of prescribed goods.
